mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) signals an accommodative monetary policy stance, reducing discount rates for equity valuations and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in declining FEDFUNDS periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeds 2.0%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 2.0%, or the Rank IC for the signal is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and increase in non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) signals a tightening labor market, which typically precedes stronger consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (PAYEMS rising and UNRATE falling) fails to produce positive 60-day returns in > 60% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In the late-cycle expansion regime (defined by year-over-year GDP growth exceeding 2.5%), the S&P 500 tends to underperform due to elevated valuations and the likelihood of monetary policy tightening, resulting in negative 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances during late-cycle expansion (GDPC1 growth > 2.5% yoy), or the Rank IC for the regime is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A low unemployment rate (UNRATE < 3.5%) signals a tight labor market, which may lead to wage inflation and subsequent Federal Reserve rate hikes, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances where UNRATE < 3.5%, or the Rank IC for the signal is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) signals weakening residential construction activity, which is a leading indicator of reduced consumer spending and economic slowdown, driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when HOUST declines, or the Rank IC for the signal is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) combined with slowing GDP growth (GDPC1) signals a weakening manufacturing sector and broader economic contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint signal (INDPRO decline and GDPC1 slowdown) fails to produce negative 60-day returns in > 60% of cases, or the Rank IC for the interaction is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During a monetary tightening cycle (as indicated by rising FEDFUNDS), the S&P 500 experiences negative forward returns over the next 20 trading days due to higher discount rates and reduced risk appetite.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances during monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS rising), or the Rank IC for the regime is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
